\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Two Point}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Reverse.TwoPoint
\section{Overview}
Generalized binomial coefficients yield the normalized reverse two-point estimate. Positive homogeneity and continuity extend the result to all nonnegative one-bit functions.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Generalized binomial series]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hasSum_choose_rpow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,x\in\bbr$ with $|x|<1$, the generalized binomial series converges and $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\binom{s}{k}x^k=(1+x)^s$, where $\binom{s}{k}=s(s-1)\cdots(s-k+1)/k!$ and $\binom{s}{0}=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Summability of the even binomial series]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.summable_choose_even}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hasSum_choose_rpow}
\difficulty{1}
For every $s,x\in\bbr$ with $|x|<1$, the series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\binom{s}{2k}x^{2k}$ is summable, with generalized binomial coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Even part of the binomial expansion]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.even_part_rpow_eq_tsum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hasSum_choose_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.summable_choose_even}
\difficulty{5}
Let $s,x\in\bbr$ with $|x|<1$, $((1+x)^s+(1-x)^s)/2=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\binom{s}{2k}x^{2k}$, using generalized binomial coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Moment of a positive affine bit function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_affine}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_true, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,b\in\bbr$ with $|b|<1$, uniform one-bit expectation satisfies $\E_{t\in\{0,1\}}|1+b(-1)^t|^s=((1+b)^s+(1-b)^s)/2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second generalized binomial coefficient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_two}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $s\in\bbr$, the generalized binomial coefficient satisfies $\binom{s}{2}=s(s-1)/2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recurrence between even binomial coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_even_succ}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s\in\bbr$ and $k\in\mathbb N$, the generalized binomial coefficients satisfy $\binom{s}{2k+2}=\binom{s}{2k}(s-2k)(s-2k-1)/((2k+1)(2k+2))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Signs of even binomial coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_even_nonpos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_even_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_two}
\difficulty{4}
Let $0<s<1$. For every integer $k\ge1$, the generalized binomial coefficient satisfies $\binom{s}{2k}\le0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borell scalar factor estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.borell_factor_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and $m\in\mathbb N$ with $m\ge2$. Then $\rho(m-q)\le m-p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Successor comparison of even coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.choose_even_ratio_step}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.borell_factor_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_even_nonpos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_even_succ}
\difficulty{5}
Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and integer $K\ge1$. If $\binom p{2K}\le(p/q)\binom q{2K}\rho^{2K}$, then $\binom p{2K+2}\le(p/q)\binom q{2K+2}\rho^{2K+2}$, with generalized binomial coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison of even binomial coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.choose_even_ratio_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.choose_even_ratio_step, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ring_choose_two}
\difficulty{4}
Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. For every integer $k\ge1$, $\binom p{2k}\le(p/q)\binom q{2k}\rho^{2k}$, with generalized binomial coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Normalized reverse two-point inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_two_point_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.choose_even_ratio_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.even_part_rpow_eq_tsum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_affine, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_affine_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.summable_choose_even, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{6}
Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and $|a|<1$. For $f(t)=1+a(-1)^t$ on $\{0,1\}$, $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The two one-bit strings]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube_one_cases}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
\difficulty{4}
Every point of $\{0,1\}^1$ is either the string whose only coordinate is $0$ or the string whose only coordinate is $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Normalizing a nonnegative one-bit function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.normalize_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube_one_cases, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative function $f:\{0,1\}\to[0,\infty)$ that is not identically zero, there exist $c>0$ and $a\in[-1,1]$ such that $f(t)=c(1+a(-1)^t)$ for both bits $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of affine one-bit means]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.continuous_lpMean_affine}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
For every $s>0$, the map $a\mapsto(\E_{t\in\{0,1\}}|1+a(-1)^t|^s)^{1/s}$ is continuous on $\bbr$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[One-bit reverse Bonami--Beckner inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.continuous_lpMean_affine, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_affine_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.normalize_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_two_point_normalized, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}

Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. Every $f:\{0,1\}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}
